protocol.status: Frozen before this round's results; adaptive research on previously inspected history, not an untouched holdout
protocol.question: Can bounded dip buying or holding positive trends outperform both SPY and gold without the original grid's drawdown?
protocol.primary_reason: Diversification, trend exits and volatility sizing have prior published motivation; this is a different strategy from the TikTok grid
protocol.warmup: 2019 gold quotes; all candidates and benchmarks start together in 2020 or 2022
protocol.signals: Previous completed US-session close only; orders at next session open; weekly rules rebalance on first session of each ISO week
protocol.gold_execution: Funded gold spot proxy with 0.4% annual holding drag, not the earlier fully financed CFD; portfolio prices sampled at US open/close from minute bid/ask midpoints
protocol.spy_execution: Existing split/dividend-adjusted daily OHLC, with dividends implicitly reinvested; fractional units allowed
protocol.dip_rules: Above 200-session average: buy 50% of capped exposure; add 25% on each of up to two further 20-session ATR close-to-close drops. Quantity based on current equity; never double. Sell next open after close falls below average, basket equity loses 5%, or optional net gain per gold unit exceeds one entry ATR. After a loss wait 20 sessions. Trim exposure at next open if prior close exceeds cap. No intraday guaranteed stop.
protocol.trend_rules: Positive means close above trailing moving average. Gold-only holds while positive. Vol-scaled rules size using trailing 60-session covariance, target 15% annualized volatility, cap gross exposure. Diversified rule inverse-vol weights eligible gold/SPY; relative rule holds eligible asset with highest 126-session return. Rebalance weekly; no shorts.
protocol.controls_rules: Unleveraged single-asset controls buy and hold. Mix and leveraged single assets rebalance monthly. Same trade, gold holding and borrowing assumptions.
protocol.pass_rule: Higher after-cost ending equity than BOTH unleveraged benchmarks in BOTH start periods, daily-close drawdown <=25% in BOTH, and no reliance solely on leverage versus same-cap mix. This is a research screen, not confidence of future outperformance.

robustness.annual_walk_forward: Starting 2023, choose among the 11 fixed strategies using only 2020 through previous December: highest CAGR among positive-return rules with <=25% close drawdown, else cash. Do not describe reused history as untouched.

limitations: No historical taxes or broker-specific availability
Gold fund proxy is not a traded ETF history
No modern LLM asked to predict historical prices from hindsight

redesign.excluded_stress: Extra execution latency on stateful dip rules; requires pending-order model

summary.name: walk_forward
summary.note: Each year starts from cash after prior year-end liquidation at modeled exit cost; fixed rule chosen only on earlier years.

protocol.status: Adaptive second round, fixed after redesign_results.json: trend exits reduced drawdown but surrendered recent gold gains; no untouched-data claim
protocol.hypothesis: Keep both assets invested, size by their volatility and correlation, and reduce exposure during turbulence instead of making binary trend exits
protocol.rules: Inverse 60-session volatility weights for SPY and gold, full covariance portfolio-volatility sizing, weekly next-open rebalancing, gross exposure capped at 1.5x/2x. No trend signal, shorts, doubling, cash top-ups or stop guarantees. Target volatility is not a drawdown limit.
checks: 5% and 10% borrowing; 10 and 30 bps per side
One additional session of execution delay
protocol.etf_adjustment: Adjust all OHLC by Adj Close/Close; gold ETF expense already embedded, so do not subtract extra 0.4%
protocol.selection: Report all four. Do not promote the best-looking row as a validated winner.
protocol.success: Same screen as first redesign: beat both benchmarks in both recent starts with <=25% daily-close drawdown. Also report old-period and cost failures, plus same-cap static controls.
